comment: Single source of every permission string (00 §2, 02 D2). `permissions[]` is the platform catalogue seeded into `public.permission`; `roles[]` are the built-in roles seeded into `public.role` / `public.role_permission` (owner 02.2.1-T1, migration 0010). `resource` + `action` must equal `code` (`resource:action`, lower_snake). `sensitive` marks a permission that gates secret-adjacent data or returns a plaintext secret once; `reserved` marks a catalogue-only string whose first consumer is a V2/V3 story (V1 has no endpoint or handler for it); `tenant_assignable=false` marks a code a member principal must never hold (T79): a custom role containing one is rejected 422 `permission_not_assignable`, and the evaluator filters them out of a member's grant set. `admin` marks an administrative code (membership/role management, tenant-wide settings, secrets, policy, audit and security reads): an automation token is denied every one of them. `token_denied[]` is that deny set — exact codes or `resource:*` wildcards — and its expansion must equal the `admin`-flagged codes. The C# constants and the token deny set are generated from this file by scripts/generate-permissions.py; editing this file without regenerating fails scripts/check-permissions-drift.sh.

roles.name: Viewer
roles.description: Read granted reports. No secrets: no `sensitive` permission and no non-assignable code (00 §2).

roles.name: QA engineer
roles.description: Drafts, runs and triage. Cannot change release policy (00 §2): no `policy:write`, no case/suite/fixture write (03 §4.5).

roles.name: Test maintainer
roles.description: Approves tests and healing; owns case/suite/fixture writes and quarantine writes (00 §2, 03 §4.5, 07.3.1). Cannot approve a sensitive candidate they authored (DECISIONS §5.5) — a two-person rule enforced by the approval flow, not by a permission.

roles.name: Release approver
roles.description: Owns policy revisions and waivers (00 §2, 07). A waiver never changes a test result.

roles.name: Tenant admin
roles.description: Membership, integrations and quota (00 §2). Secret values are never readable: no `artifact:read_sensitive` and no `billing:*`. Policy stays with `release_approver` (the org creator holds both, T98).

roles.name: CI producer
roles.description: Service identity minted per CI job for exactly one project: {run:create, event:write, artifact:write, decision:read} (FR-02-7, AC4). It reads the decision of its own project's runs, so a CI gate can wait for one, and cannot approve, read another project or change policy.

roles.name: Agent
roles.description: Service identity per (tenant, pool) (V2, 02.5): claimed jobs and uploads in its pool only — no approvals, policy or other projects (00 §2).

roles.name: Platform operator
roles.description: Evidgate staff. No standing tenant access: support access needs a scope + expiry grant the tenant approves (FR-02-13).

roles.name: Billing operator
roles.description: Evidgate staff. Reads the usage ledger and invoice data across tenants, audited; no artifact or test data access (00 §2, 12).

permissions.description: Read agent pool definitions and their capability match (V2, 05.7.3).
Create or change an agent pool (V2, 05.7.3).
Request an AI-generated case/suite draft (V2, 03.6.x). The draft is never gate-eligible.
List project API-token metadata (id, name, prefix, permissions, status, last_used_at) — never the secret or its HMAC (02.4.4).
Create or revoke a project API token; the plaintext secret is returned exactly once (02.4.4).
Read artifact metadata and obtain a short-lived download URL (00 §9.3).
Read artifact content classified `sensitive` (traces, DOM/a11y snapshots) on every path that can return it; each issuance is audited (00 §7, 06.2.1).
Request an upload URL and complete an upload for a run/attempt (00 §9.3).
Read and export the tenant audit log, support-grant actions included (00 §9.3, 02.7.1).
Generate authoring content — feature nodes, checklist items and manual test cases — from an imported or AI-drafted source (13.3.1). Generation spends AI credits (08.5.5), so it is its own code.
Read the feature tree, its checklist items and its manual test cases (00 §2, 13.1.1).
Create, change, reorder, move, retire and delete feature nodes, checklist items and manual test cases (00 §2, 13.1.1).
Read the usage ledger and invoice data across tenants (staff only, every read audited; 00 §2, 12).
Load price cards, adjust the ledger and issue statements on the operator ingress; adjustments and statements are two-person (12, T69).
Read the case catalog and case revisions (00 §9.3, 03).
Write case revisions in the catalog (03 §4.5).
Create, change or disable a project CI binding, including the one-time repository challenge (02.4.1).
Read a run's or release's exact evaluation revision and its reasons (00 §9.3, 07).
Run a sandbox dry run of a draft (V2, 03.6.1).
Open a pull/merge request from a draft, idempotent by (branch, commit) (V2, 03.6.1).
Create and edit authoring drafts (V2, 03.6.1). A draft is never gate-eligible.
Create an immutable environment revision (00 §9.3, 05.1.2).
Send an event batch for a run and finalize a producer shard (00 §9.3). Service identities only: the CI producer or the agent (04, 05).
Write fixture revisions (03 §4.5). Reading a fixture reuses `suite:read` (T56).
Approve, reject or revoke a healing candidate, bound to candidate_hash + base commit (V2, 00 §8.7, 08).
Change the healing kill switch for the tenant/project; the most restrictive scope wins (00 §8.7, 08.6.3).
Revoke an approved candidate or a knowledge record, blocking future use (V2, 00 §8.7, 08).
Read incidents and candidates, label an incident and set the kill switch's read side (00 §2, 08). Human labels are the only ground truth.
List project ingest-token metadata (id, name, prefix, status, last_used_at) — never the secret or its HMAC (02.4.2).
Create, rotate or revoke a project ingest token; the plaintext secret is returned exactly once (02.4.2).
Claim a queued job matching the agent's pool and capability (V2, 00 §9.3, 05.7).
Run a side-effecting job cleanup, e.g. abandoning a lease or purging a cancelled job's workspace (V2).
Heartbeat the current job lease and report its execution events (V2, 00 §9.3, 05.7).
Read org memberships and pending invites (02 §4.2, T59).
Invite, change the roles of or remove a member; the last-admin guard rejects removing the last tenant_admin (02.1.2).
Read the organizations the caller is a member of, and one organization's settings (02.1.1).
Create an organization and change its settings (slug, retention default, allowed email domains) (02.1.1).
Read policy revisions, waivers and quarantine entries — open to every member role, viewer included, so an exception is never hidden (T58, 07.1.1).
Create or activate a policy revision and create/approve/revoke a waiver (00 §2, 07).
Create a project in an org (org-level, not per-project; 00 §9.3, T21).
Read project settings such as retention and capture options (T21: every member role).
Change project settings such as retention and the artifact kind policy (T21: tenant_admin).
Create or remove a quarantine entry; never for a case on the active policy's critical list (T23, 07.3.1).
Read the permission catalogue and the built-in roles (any member; 02.2.1).
Create or change a custom role; built-in roles are immutable (409 builtin_role_immutable) and non-assignable codes are rejected (422 permission_not_assignable) (02.2.1).
Record a cancel request for a run; a cancelled run never becomes complete (00 §8.1, 05.4.1).
Upload a manifest, create a run, rerun or reprocess, and bind a run to a release (00 §9.3).
Read run state, the evidence revision, report comparisons and environment revisions (00 §9.3).
Generate a test script from a manual test case and open it against the customer repository as a pull request (13.5.1).
Read the org's security events: auth failures and support access in V1, injection attempts from V2 (00 §9.3, 11.5.1).
List agent service identities of the tenant (V2, 02.5).
Create, rotate or revoke an agent service identity (V2, 02.5).
Read the org's SAML/SSO connection (V3, 02.3.3).
Create, change or remove the org's SAML/SSO connection (V3, 02.3.3).
Read suite revisions, their diffs and the fixtures they reference (00 §9.3, T56).
Write suite revisions (03 §4.5). A published revision is immutable.
Approve or revoke a support grant for the caller's org; approver ≠ requester (00 §9.3, 02.8.1).
Request operator access with scope, reason and expiry on the operator session (00 §9.3, 02.8.1).
Read support grants: the tenant's own grants, or the operator's own requests (T59, 02.8.1).
Read the org's usage summary (counters vs quota) and ledger (00 §9.3, 12).
Read outbound webhook endpoints and their delivery log, never the signing secret (T61, 07.6.2).
Create, change or delete an outbound webhook endpoint; https only, SSRF-blocked targets (T61, 07.6.2).
